prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses is based on management’s assessment of the adequacy of the allowance for credit losses. Factors impacting the provision include inherent risk characteristics in our loan portfolio, the level of nonperforming loans and net charge-offs, both current and historic, economic and credit conditions, the direction of the change in collateral values, and the funding probability associated with unfunded loan commitments. The provision for credit losses is recorded as a charge against current period earnings in order to maintain our allowance for credit losses, which reflects management’s best estimate of current expected credit losses in our loan portfolio at the balance sheet date.

The provision for credit losses for both loans and unfunded loan commitments was $7 thousand and $1.2 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $3.5 million and $5.5 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The provision for credit losses for loans for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, can be attributed to several factors including organic loan growth and changes in portfolio mix and an increase in the ACL for certain individually evaluated loans.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table sets forth the various components of our noninterest expense for the periods indicated:

Total noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $16.3 million, compared to $15.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $763 thousand, or 4.9%. The increase can be attributed to higher salaries and employee benefits, higher occupancy and furniture and equipment costs, an increase in professional fees, and higher other expenses. The $360 thousand increase in salaries and employee benefits is attributed to higher commissions expense as well as slightly higher employee salaries and stock-based compensation costs. These increases were partially offset by higher salary deferrals associated with increased loan originations in 2026, lower group insurance costs, and a slight decrease in various other salaries and benefits related expenses. The combined $288 thousand increase in occupancy and furniture and equipment costs can be attributed primarily to our expansion into the San Jose and San Mateo markets. The $150 thousand increase in professional fees was due to expenses incurred related to Bancorp becoming an SEC registrant and a Nasdaq-listed company during the third quarter of 2026.

tax.text: Provision for income taxes for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $5.4 million and $16.3 million, respectively, compared to $4.9 million and $14.9 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The effective tax rate was 24.43% and 27.10% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to 28.79% and 28.88% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The decrease in the effective tax rate for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the same periods in 2025 was primarily attributable to a $920 thousand income tax benefit resulting from the Company’s purchase of transferable renewable energy tax credits at a discount during the third quarter of 2026, as well as an increase in tax-exempt interest income on loans when compared to 2025.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text:
Net income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $16.7 million and $43.9 million, respectively, compared to net income of $12.1 million and $36.7 million, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively, reflecting increases of $4.7 million, or 38.8%, and $7.2 million, or 19.7%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025. Diluted EPS for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, were $1.59 and $4.17, respectively, compared to $1.14 and $3.45 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively.

Net income and diluted EPS for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, increased compared to the same periods in 2025 primarily due to higher net interest income stemming from growth in average interest-earning assets, a reduction in the provision for credit losses on loans, and higher noninterest income during 2026. In addition, net income and diluted EPS for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, reflect a $920 thousand income tax benefit recorded in the third quarter of 2026 related to the purchase of $16.0 million of transferable renewable energy tax credits at a discount. The benefit increased diluted EPS by approximately $0.09 during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

sbc.text: The effective tax rate differs from the federal statutory rate primarily due to the impact of state taxes as well as the mix and amount of various permanent tax differences, including tax-exempt income from municipal securities, loans and bank-owned life insurance policies, tax benefits associated with low-income housing tax credit investments, tax benefits associated with the purchase of transferable renewable energy tax credits, and stock-based compensation, among others.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, net interest income totaled $37.1 million, reflecting an increase of $2.5 million, or 7.1%, from $34.6 million for the same period in 2025. Taxable-equivalent net interest income, a non-GAAP measure, totaled $37.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $2.5 million, or 7.3%, from $34.8 million for the same period in 2025. The year-over-year increase in net interest income was primarily attributable to growth in interest income stemming from overall higher average interest-earning assets, including a $191.4 million increase in average loan balances. Growth in interest income was partially offset by an increase in interest expense largely associated with a $244.5 million year-over-year increase in average money market deposit balances.

The net interest margin was 5.18% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 5.26% for the same period ended in 2025. The taxable equivalent net interest margin, a non-GAAP financial measure, was 5.20% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 5.28% for the same period ended in 2025.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
The following table sets forth the various components of our noninterest income for the periods indicated:

Total noninterest income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $1.3 million and $5.2 million, respectively, compared to $1.3 million and $3.7 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively, representing an increase of approximately $18 thousand, or 1.4% and $1.5 million, or 40.9%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025. The increase in noninterest income for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, is largely attributed to $153 thousand and $521 thousand of special dividends received on our holdings of Federal Home Loan Bank (“FHLB”) of San Francisco stock during the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, increases in service charges on deposits due to growth in deposit balances, and an increase in earnings on bank-owned life insurance during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. The increase in total noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, is also attributable to a $912 thousand gain on the sale of non-core residential loans that were acquired in the merger with 1 st Capital Bancorp in 2024 recognized during the first quarter of 2026.
